Use case: precise-object-edit. Project asset: registered HEWRS suit garment overlay, not a new outfit or person.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: an existing jacket-and-trousers-only transparent PNG on a 996 by 2748 pixel canvas. Image 2 is a PRIVATE FABRIC REFERENCE ONLY. Change only the COLOR and FINE CLOTH PATTERN of the jacket and trousers in image 1 to match the real suit in image 2.
S02: reference photo 2 is the real suit worn with a pale yellow tie and tan shoes. The suit is charcoal/medium-dark gray, neutral to very slightly warm under indoor light, with an extremely understated low-contrast tonal rectangular/Glen check. Current edit target is incorrectly brown/taupe with prominent pale plaid bands. Correct to the photographed muted charcoal gray with much quieter very fine tonal checks; remove strong light horizontal/vertical bands. Preserve the sophisticated woven cloth shading and original garment construction. Do NOT make it a solid black suit or bright gray. Both trousers and jacket have identical cloth.
ABSOLUTE GEOMETRY LOCK: reproduce image 1's same canvas aspect ratio and composition including the substantial empty transparent head area above the collar and transparent feet area below trouser hems. Keep the exact same silhouette, shoulders, arm positions, sleeve lengths, lapel shapes and location, two buttons in the same locations, breast welt pocket, both hip flap pockets, hem, trouser shape, creases, leg spacing, and all original holes for hands and shirt. Do not resize the garment within the frame, do not center or crop it differently, do not change pose or tailoring. Output only the same garment cutout; NO head, face, person, skin, hands, shirt, tie, watch, belt, shoes, surroundings, labels, text or watermarks. The shirt/neck aperture, hand gaps, background, area above shoulders and area below hems must all be truly transparent. Reference image 2 controls fabric appearance only, never body shape, identity, pose, accessories, clothing cut, or background. Preserve original shading and three-dimensional cloth construction while replacing only the inaccurate fabric appearance. Highly faithful photographic cloth texture, no painterly blur.

Use case: precise-object-edit. This is a second corrective pass on the S13 transparent suit garment overlay for a frozen-avatar wardrobe app. Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the generated jacket+trousers-only cutout. Input image 2 is the actual clothing PHOTO REFERENCE. Change ONLY the fabric PATTERN: the current gray-blue charcoal color is already close, so preserve that palette and current tailoring/shading. The current pattern is too busy, irregular, wiggly and high contrast. Replace it with the quieter, geometrically regular, finely woven Glen/plaid check actually visible in the photograph: grouped fine DARK threads in mostly straight vertical and horizontal lines, subtle rectangles, a calm low-contrast ground. Match the cloth exactly as observed on the photo's chest and upper trousers. Reduce the excessive high-frequency busy/wormy/maze-like line texture by about one third and regularize its direction; preserve fabric weave detail without blurred noise. Pattern should follow real cloth folds only, not wander chaotically. No bright pale lines, no conspicuous giant windowpane, no pinstripes, no plain solid suit. Jacket and trousers must use the same cloth.
ABSOLUTE LOCK: same transparent canvas aspect, empty head and foot margins, same locations and shapes of shoulders, arms, lapels, breast pocket, flap pockets, buttons, jacket hem, trouser legs and hand-shaped holes as image 1. Do not add a person, head, face, skin, hands, shirt, tie, belt, shoes, text, watermark, backdrop or props. Do not change pose, silhouette, placement, proportions or crop. This is only a quiet, regular, fine plaid fabric-pattern correction. Output a truly transparent PNG, same composition as the edit target.
